topic: Why Can We See Through Glass But Not Through a Wall?
script:
Why can you see through a window, but not through a brick wall? Both are solid, yet light behaves very differently when it meets them.

Visible light passes through ordinary clear glass because its electrons do not strongly absorb most visible wavelengths. The light can travel onward to your eyes.

But glass still reflects a little light at each surface. That is why you can sometimes see your own face in a dark window.

A brick wall is different. Its pigments and uneven internal structure absorb and scatter visible light, so a clear image cannot pass through.

And frosted glass reveals the final trick. It lets light through, but its rough surface scatters the rays in many directions, turning sharp details into a blur.
